title: Apollo 1 (1967)
summary: A fire in the Apollo 1 command module during a launch-pad test killed all three crew. NASA's page says it spread quickly in the pure-oxygen atmosphere and the hatch could not be opened in time. Afterwards NASA fitted a hatch that opens in three seconds, restricted combustible materials and used fire-resistant materials in new spacesuits.
caveat: Summary of NASA's page. It is the reason atmosphere and material choice matter in this app.

title: Apollo 13 (1970)
summary: An oxygen tank exploded on the third day of flight and the crew abandoned the lunar landing. NASA's page links it to tank insulation damaged when heaters ran during a launch-pad test. Later missions added a third oxygen tank, upgraded thermostats, removed stirring fans and sheathed wiring.
caveat: An oxygen-system failure, not a cabin fire. It shows how oxygen storage can become the hazard.

title: Mir fire (1997)
summary: A solid-fuel oxygen generator ignited on Mir. The flame lasted several minutes, blocked access to a Soyuz escape vehicle and filled the station with smoke. The crew wore oxygen masks and used foam extinguishers. NASA's page says the lessons changed crew training, ground responses and canister preparation, and fed into ISS design.
source_title: NASA: 25 Years Ago, Fire Aboard Space Station Mir
caveat: The page says investigators believe latex glove material in the canister was the most likely cause.

title: Smoke detector that tells smoke from dust
summary: A 1970s detector developed for the shuttle samples air for combustion particles and distinguishes them from dust, so it raises fewer false alarms. NASA's page suggests uses such as protecting large areas like mines.
caveat: The page gives no developer name beyond an earlier detector it builds on.

title: Lighter firefighter air tank
summary: A backpack air tank developed with NASA's Johnson Space Center, about 20 pounds with a 30-minute air supply. It uses an aluminum liner wrapped in resin-impregnated glass fibre at 4,500 psi and is 13 pounds lighter than conventional tanks.
caveat: Figures are as stated on NASA's 1970s spin-off page.

title: Firefighter protective clothing
summary: Project FIRES, a NASA and FEMA U.S. Fire Administration program, produced a protective ensemble using lightweight, heat-protective materials first developed for astronaut spacesuits and spacecraft thermal protection.
source_title: NASA Spinoff: New Technology for the Fire Attire
